text:
Come to my breast, deaf and cruel soul,
Beloved tiger, monster of indolent air;
I want to bury my trembling fingers
In the thicket of your abundant mane;


To bury my aching head
In your lap full of perfume
And breathe, like a withered flower,
The night dew of my extinguished love.


I want to sleep! To sleep more than to live!
In a dream, sweet as death,
I shall press my kisses without rest
Upon your body polished like copper.


To drown my muffled sobs,
I need only your profound bed;
Powerful oblivion dwells between your lips
And Lethe flows from your kisses.


My fate, henceforth my delight,
Like a predestined man I shall follow;
An innocent condemned man, a docile martyr
Whose fervor increases in torment.


To drown my rancor, I shall drain
The nepenthe and beloved hemlock
From the delicious nipple crowning this breast
Which never held a heart.

translation.title: Lethe
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Baudelaire’s French original; the source footnote marker is omitted as bibliographic matter.
